instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 364 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Draft:

Dear Principal,

I am writing about the proposal to require community service from every student. I think you should not require it, though I hope the school will keep encouraging it and make it easier to do.

My main reason is that service only works when the person doing it wants to be there. My friend Dana tutors second graders in reading twice a week. She knows which kids are stuck on which sounds, and she brings in books about sharks for one boy because sharks are the only thing he will read about. Now picture a student who was sent there to fill a requirement and is watching the clock. A seven-year-old can tell the difference. The child gets a worse tutor, and the student learns that helping people is one more chore to finish before graduation.

My second reason is time, which is not shared equally among students. Some of my classmates have free afternoons. Others work at a grocery store until nine, or go home to watch younger brothers and sisters until a parent finishes a shift. Those students are already serving somebody, and their families depend on it. A flat requirement of forty hours would cost them much more than it costs a student with nothing scheduled after the last bell. Some would have to choose between a paycheck and a diploma, and that is not a choice a school should force.

I also worry about what happens to the places we would be sent. The food pantry near my house has two paid staff members. If sixty teenagers arrive needing signatures, those two people spend the afternoon inventing tasks and filling in forms. The litter crews my friends join on Saturdays are useful because ten willing people show up with gloves and bags.

There is a better option. Offer service as an elective credit, let clubs organize projects during the school day, and recognize students who put in real hours at graduation. Count the work students already do for their families. That would bring in more volunteers without punishing anyone who cannot spare the time.

Thank you for considering a student's view before you decide.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
